REGENT OF SUMEDANG WEST JAVA PROVINCE
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SUMEDANG REGENCY
NUMBER 5 OF 2024
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
THE REGENT OF SUMEDANG. Considering :
a. that every person has the right to be free from discriminatory treatment and to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in various fields of development in Sumedang Regency; b. the child is one of the implementations of concurrent government affairs policies that are the authority of regional government, which constitutes an integral dimension unity starting from planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, supervision and reporting on policies, programs, and regional development activities; c. that to realize legal certainty and provide legal protection guarantees as well as synergy and integration in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Sumedang Regency Region, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to stipulate a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection; In View of : 1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. KTP.
Article 41
Further provisions regarding the prevention of Violence against women involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 38 through Article 40, shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Children Requiring Special Protection hereinafter abbreviated as AMPK are Children in emergency situations, Children in conflict with the law, Children from minority and isolated groups, Children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, Children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse, Children who are victims of pornography, Children with HIV/AIDS, Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, and/or trafficking, Children who are victims of physical and/or psychological violence, Children who are victims of sexual crimes, Children who are victims of terrorist networks, Children with disabilities, Children who are victims of abuse and neglect, Children with deviant social behavior, and Children who are victims of stigmatization from labeling related to their parents' condition, and Children with other problems. 30. Gender Data is data regarding the relationship of relations in status, roles, and conditions between men and women. 31. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of Gender and Child Data consisting of components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/institutions and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of Gender Responsive and child-caring development. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree. 33. Family Quality is the condition of the Family determined by the dimensions of quality of legality and structure, quality of physical resilience, quality of economic resilience, quality of socio-psychological resilience, and quality of socio-cultural resilience in realizing Gender Equality and Child Rights. 34. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and preventing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 35. Violence Against Women hereinafter abbreviated as KTP is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 36. Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 38. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, resulting from the criminal act of human trafficking. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body that in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 43. Business World is micro business, small business, medium business, and large business that conducts economic activities in Indonesia and is domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45. Community Participation is the role of community members to channel their aspirations, thoughts, and interests in the administration of Regional Government. 46. Community Organization hereinafter referred to as Ormas is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities, and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 47. Social Conflict hereinafter referred to as Conflict is a feud and/or physical clash with Violence between two or more community groups that lasts for a certain time and has broad impacts resulting in insecurity and social disintegration thus disrupting national stability and hindering national development. 48. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit formed by the Regional Government in providing services for women and Children who experience Violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems. 49.

Article 39
(1) Prevention of KTP involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 37 letter a, shall be implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
(2) Standards for KTP prevention as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. institutional implementers of KTP prevention in the Regency Area;
b. understanding of KTP; and
c. integration of KTP prevention policies across all development sectors.
(3) Procedures for KTP prevention as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. coordination and synchronization of implementation of policies, programs, and activities for KTP prevention in the Regency Area, consisting of:
1. issuing regulations on KTP prevention involving parties in the Regency Area, covering primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention;
2. socialization and advocacy on KTP to policy makers and other stakeholders in the Regency Area; and
3. building cooperation for KTP prevention involving parties in the Regency Area.
b. policy advocacy and service assistance for Women's Protection in the Regency Area, covering:
1. building commitment in KTP prevention;
2. integrating KTP prevention into the Regency regional development planning; and
3. encouraging increased Community Participation and cooperation with the Business Sector and mass media in KTP prevention.

Part Five
Protection of Women From Gender-Based Violence In Disasters

Seventh Part Implementation
Paragraph 1 Scope
Article 37
The Implementation of Women's Protection in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 21 paragraph (1), consists of:
a. prevention of KTP involving parties in the Regency Area;
b. provision of services for women victims of Violence requiring coordination in the Regency Area; and
c. strengthening and development of Women's Protection Service Provider Institutions in the Regency Area.

Article 72
(1) Prevention of KTA involving parties in the Regency Region as referred to in Article 70 letter a shall be implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
(2) Standards for prevention of KTA involving parties in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) Procedures for prevention of KTA involving parties in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of:
a. development and strengthening of institutional framework for KTA prevention;
b. policy advocacy and assistance or technical guidance for implementation of policies, programs, and activities for KTA prevention in the Regency Region; and

Part Three Protection of Women in Conflict
Article 23
(1) The Regency Regional Government implements protection for women in Conflict.
(2) The Regency Regional Government in implementing protection for women in Conflict as referred to in paragraph (1), must pay attention to the conditions, situation, problems, and handling of Conflict in the Regency Region.
(3) Protection of women in Conflict as referred to in paragraph (1), consists of:
a. prevention; and
b. provision of services.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Part One Definitions
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data according to sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and fulfilling their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self, resulting in, or likely to result in, physical, psychological, and sexual harm or suffering to women and children, including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal actions, and other actions to ensure Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment rights and alternative care, basic health rights and welfare, as well as education rights, use of leisure time, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Part Two Improvement of Family Quality in Realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas
Article 83 Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas is implemented through:
a. implementation of policies, programs, and activities; and
b. development of materials and implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families.
(1) Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas is implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
(2) Standards for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. institutional arrangements;
b. availability of communication, information, and education materials;
c. synergy and coordination; and
d. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
(3) Procedures for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of:
a. policy advocacy and family assistance to realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights in Regency Areas include:
1. preparation of planning and budgeting documents for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
2. coordination and synchronization of policy formulation for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
3. increasing Community Participation and mass media in improving Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights; and
4. strengthening cooperation of Regency Regional Apparatus to realize Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights.
b. implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families in Regency Areas; and
c. development of Community activities for improving Family Quality in Regency Areas.

Article 35
The Regency Regional Government in implementing the protection of women with disabilities as referred to in Article 34, shall:
a. provide information service units and rapid response for women with disabilities who are victims of Violence;
b. provide Special Protection for women with disabilities; and
c. provide accessible safe houses for women with disabilities.

4.3.rationale: The original Indonesian text DOES include primary-prevention activities that are explicitly about the legal/policy framework on violence against women (VAW). In Pasal 39 ayat (3) huruf a angka 1 it states: “menerbitkan regulasi tentang pencegahan KTP … meliputi pencegahan primer, sekunder, dan tersier;” and in angka 2: “sosialisasi dan advokasi tentang KTP kepada pengambil kebijakan dan pemangku kepentingan lainnya…”. This is awareness-raising/socialization and advocacy about the KTP prevention regulation/policy itself (i.e., the legal/policy framework), which matches the indicator’s intent (VAW laws/policies awareness as primary prevention). The retrieved English candidates included this content (candidate [4.3-46] Article 39(3) explicitly mentions “issuing regulations” and “socialization and advocacy on KTP”), so a correct judge could have answered Yes. The judge was overly strict by requiring an explicit phrase like “laws and policies” and ignoring that “issuing regulations” plus “socialization and advocacy” about KTP is exactly legal/policy awareness activity.

b. policy advocacy and service assistance for Women's Protection in the Regency Area, covering:

Article 51
(1) The Regency Regional Government, the Community, the Family, and Parents or Guardians are obliged and responsible for the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.
(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the Regency Regional Government in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

b. implementing and supporting national policies in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency; and
c. providing support for facilities, infrastructure, and the availability of human resources in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency.
(3) The Regency Regional Government, in carrying out its obligations and responsibilities in Child Protection in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall do so by:
a. guaranteeing the protection, care, and welfare of Children by taking into account the rights and obligations of Parents, Guardians, or other persons who are legally responsible for Children; and

5.4.rationale: The original Indonesian Pasal 69 states the local government “menyediakan” (provides) various types of personnel for implementing Special Protection for Children, including “pendidik dan tenaga kependidikan” (educators and education personnel). This is about staffing/service provision capacity, not about engaging education institutions (schools/education sector bodies) as stakeholders/partners in planning/implementation. The judge treated the mere mention of educators as proof of stakeholder engagement, which is a category error: having educators as part of service personnel ≠ formal engagement of education institutions. The retrieved passage [5.4-78] accurately reflects Pasal 69, so the evidence available supports a No for “education institutions engagement” under a typical stakeholder-engagement definition. Therefore the discrepancy is best explained by judge misinterpretation/overly lenient reasoning, not retrieval or translation.
